title: P23-family: squared-ReLU MLP activation (Primer) instead of GELU, parameter-identical
description: P23-family (MLP activation; P23's SwiGLU was 047): replace the fork MLP's GELU with squared ReLU, fc2(relu(fc1(h))^2), with identical parameters, init and RNG streams to the 070-claude incumbent, and keep it through RL and eval. Squared ReLU gave consistent LM quality gains in Primer and is standard in Muon speedruns; sparse, multiplicative-like MLP features should represent 'this rule applies to these lines' conditions more selectively, giving expert iteration a sharper starting policy without extra compute.
hypothesis: Squared ReLU is a cheap multiplicative nonlinearity: relu(a)^2 = relu(a)*relu(a) acts like a gated unit with tied gate/value, so each MLP feature fires sparsely and grows quadratically with evidence. Primer (So et al. 2021) found this improves LM loss per compute, and it pairs with Muon in modded-nanogpt. Unlike 047's SwiGLU it keeps d_ff 1024 and every parameter shape, so Muon shape scaling, orthogonal init and step time are unchanged. If the gain transfers, pretraining reaches slightly lower val loss and RL starts from a policy that picks applicable inference rules more selectively, so more round-1 targets and more >=7 dev theorems are solved. Risk: near-zero init pre-activations (std ~0.3) put relu^2 in a low-gradient regime early and the RL stage's frozen AdamW may be less stable with quadratic activations; also the two extra elementwise kernels per block could slow sampling a few percent (070's slowest seed ran 1079 of 1200 s).
expected_delta: -40 to +30 theorems at >=7 (central +3 versus 352.67); pretraining 4700-4800 steps, final val loss within +/-3% of 070's 0.0911/0.0913/0.0961; total seconds within +60 s of 070's 1048/971/1079

arch.change: CHANGED versus 070-claude: MLP activation GELU -> squared ReLU, fc2(relu(fc1(ln2(x)))**2) (So et al. 2021, Primer). Implemented by setting each fork Block's __class__ to a Block subclass that overrides only forward; the attention/KV-cache code is inherited unchanged. Same 5 untied blocks, d_model 256, 8 heads (head dim 32), d_ff 1024, RoPE base 10000, LayerNorm, untied embedding/readout.
arch.n_params_detail: unchanged from 070-claude (no parameters added or removed): 4,000,000
arch.checkpoint_reconstruction: state dict keys identical to 070-claude; reconstructing with the fork's plain GPT(vocab, 5, 256, 8) would load but silently revert to GELU, so the harness must use the returned module object (it does)
arch.kv_cache: one fork KV-cache dict per logical block (5 per sample), unchanged fork code

optimizer.name: split-QKV Muon on hidden matrices and the output readout head.weight throughout; continuous AdamW auxiliary (unchanged from 070-claude)

muon.precision: bf16 Newton-Schulz; fp32 momentum and parameters
muon.shape_scale: sqrt(max(1, rows/columns)) per orthogonalized matrix: Q/K/V each 1, attention output 1, fc1 2, fc2 1, head (99,256) 1
muon.schedule: same warmup/cosine fraction as AdamW; muon_lr = 0.01 * adam_lr / 0.001
muon.parameters: All 20 hidden projection parameters (4 per block x 5 blocks) plus head.weight (99,256; vocab 99, no bias) are in Muon: 21 matrices. Five qkv.weight matrices of shape (768,256) use independent Q/K/V updates, represented as a batch of three (256,256) matrices; proj/fc1/fc2 and head are orthogonalized whole. head is wide (99<256) so it is not transposed and its update has 99 singular values near 1.
muon.license: MIT; full copyright and permission notice retained in pretrain.py
muon.qkv_split: After elementwise Nesterov momentum, reshape each QKV update to (3,256,256); independently Frobenius-normalize and run five batched Newton-Schulz steps; reshape back before applying. No extra learning-rate multiplier. Momentum and weight decay stay elementwise and unchanged.

optimizer.adamw_parameters: emb.weight, all projection biases and LayerNorm parameters (incl. ln_f) throughout; head.weight and hidden matrices never enter pretraining AdamW
optimizer.decay_convention: unchanged from 070-claude: MUON_WD = 10 * WD * LR / MUON_LR = 0.1 on all 21 Muon matrices; AdamW group wd 0.1
optimizer.clipping: joint global gradient norm 1.0 before both optimizers
optimizer.handoff: standard GPT weights only; pretraining optimizer states are discarded and frozen RL creates its own unchanged AdamW

config.init: Exactly 070-claude: fork default construction with 5 blocks, then orthogonal_ on every 2D block parameter (gain 0.02*sqrt(max(rows, cols))); embedding and readout keep the fork normal(0.02); biases zero. The __class__ swap draws no random numbers, so initial weights and data order/shift RNG streams per seed are identical to 070-claude (paired comparison per seed).
